documents.title: Concerns about the shared calendar
documents.text:
To: Operations team
From: Dimitri Ivanov, Team Leader
Subject: Shared calendar: new rules

Hello everyone,

Over the past month, I have noticed that the shared team calendar has become unreliable. Several meetings were booked in the same room at the same time, two client calls were scheduled during a training day, and I discovered last Thursday that nobody had recorded my own absence, so a delivery was left without a contact. I understand that it is easy to forget, but the calendar only works if everybody uses it consistently.

From Monday, I would therefore ask that you follow three simple rules. First, every meeting that involves more than two people must be entered in the calendar, with the room and the name of the organizer. Second, absences of half a day or longer should be entered at least a day in advance, using the color assigned to your role. Third, entries that are no longer valid must be deleted rather than left in place, since old entries make it harder to see what is truly planned.

I will review the calendar every Friday and send a short message to anyone whose entries are incomplete. If the situation has not improved in a month, we will discuss whether to adopt a different tool, as some teams are considering a booking program with automatic conflict warnings. Thank you for your cooperation.

Dimitri

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of the e-mail?
choices: To announce the purchase of a new program
To ask the team to use a tool more carefully
To criticize a client for late payment
To cancel a training day
questions.explanation: He sets out three rules for using the shared calendar properly.

choices: Two meetings used one room
A client call was set in the wrong week
The calendar was unavailable all day
A delivery had nobody to contact about it
questions.explanation: Nobody had recorded Mr. Ivanov's absence, so a delivery was left without a contact.

choices: Those that are out of date
Those entered by the team leader
Those with more than two attendees
Those made in the color of a role
questions.explanation: Entries no longer valid should be deleted rather than left in place.

questions.prompt: What might happen if there is no improvement?
choices: The leader will stop reviewing the calendar
The team will lose its meeting rooms
The team could change to a different system
Clients will be asked to book calls
questions.explanation: They will discuss adopting a different tool such as a booking program with automatic conflict warnings.

documents.title: A river town counts the cost of cheap flights
documents.text:
For ten years, the arrival of a low-cost airline was celebrated in the river town of Waldmere. Visitor numbers tripled, new restaurants opened, and the empty warehouses along the quay were converted into apartments. This autumn, however, the airline announced that it would withdraw from the regional airport, citing rising fees and disappointing demand in winter, and the town is now facing questions about what it has built.

The effects are already visible. Hotel owners report cancellations for the next season, and one of the largest, the Riverside, has said it will not renew its summer contracts with seasonal staff. Property agents say that the buyers of holiday apartments, many of whom live abroad, have begun to sell. "People bought because they could fly in for the weekend for twenty dollars," says agent Karen Voss. "Without the flights, there is no market."

Mayor Henrik Ljung insists that the town is not defenseless. Talks are under way with two other carriers, and the council has proposed a program to promote winter walking and cycling along the river. Economist Diana Cho, however, believes that depending on a single airline was always a mistake. "Tourism built on a subsidy of cheap travel is fragile by definition," she says. "The question is whether Waldmere has anything left to offer when the discount disappears."

questions.prompt: What is the main subject of the article?
choices: The success of a recently opened hotel on the river
A plan to build a second airport nearby
The risks facing a town after losing an airline
The rise of cycling holidays throughout Europe
questions.explanation: The airline's withdrawal threatens a tourism economy built on cheap flights.

questions.prompt: Why did the airline decide to leave?
choices: Costs rose and winter demand was weak
The town refused to build more hotels
Its planes were not allowed to land at night
It was bought by another company
questions.explanation: The airline cited rising fees and disappointing demand in winter.

questions.prompt: What is suggested by Ms. Voss's comment?
choices: Local people are refusing to buy any apartments
Flights to the town had always been expensive
Property prices will soon rise sharply again
Many owners bought homes mainly for the cheap flights
questions.explanation: People bought because they could fly in cheaply; without the flights there is no market.

questions.prompt: The word "fragile" in the last paragraph is closest in meaning to
choices: extremely popular
easily damaged
well organized
slow to change
questions.explanation: Tourism that depends on a single subsidy can easily be damaged when it disappears.

documents.title: Parking changes near Greenfield Station
documents.text:
Following a review of the parking provision around Greenfield Station, the council has approved changes that will take effect on 1 September. The two car parks on Station Road, which are currently free for the first two hours, will in future charge 1.50 dollars per hour, with a daily maximum of 9 dollars. Season tickets for regular commuters will be available at 120 dollars per month from the ticket office or online. Residents of Station Road and Alma Street, where permits are already required, will be given two free visitor permits per year.

The council's review found that more than half of the spaces were being occupied all day by commuters, leaving little room for shoppers and visitors to the nearby market. The income raised will be used to improve the cycle shelter, which will be doubled in size and fitted with lighting, and to fund a new bus service between the station and the Eastfield estate, which is due to begin in January.

Blue Badge holders will continue to park free of charge in the marked bays beside the entrance. Anyone who parks without paying will receive a penalty of 45 dollars, reduced to 25 dollars if paid within fourteen days. A public information session will take place at the library on 12 August at 7 p.m. Comments may be submitted by e-mail to parking@greenfieldcouncil.example before 20 August.

questions.prompt: What is the main reason for the change?
choices: The car parks were losing money in every year
Commuters were filling most spaces all day long
The station was going to be rebuilt for the market
Residents had complained about noise at night
questions.explanation: More than half of the spaces were taken all day by commuters, leaving little room for shoppers and visitors.

questions.prompt: What will the money from the charges pay for?
choices: Repairs to the surface of the road outside the station
More staff to work at the station ticket office
Free parking spaces for the traders at the market
Improved facilities for cyclists and a new bus route
questions.explanation: It will improve the cycle shelter and fund a new bus service.

questions.prompt: Who will still be able to park free of charge?
choices: Holders of a Blue Badge in the marked bays
Commuters who leave their cars all day
Shoppers who stay for more than two hours
Residents of the new Eastfield estate
questions.explanation: Blue Badge holders will continue to park free of charge in the marked bays beside the entrance.

questions.prompt: What can be inferred about a driver who pays a fine on day ten?
choices: The driver will pay 45 dollars
The driver will not have to pay
The driver will pay 25 dollars
The driver will lose the visitor permit
questions.explanation: The penalty is reduced to 25 dollars if paid within fourteen days.
